examples.en: I hurt my leg, so I walk with a waddle.
The bear lumbered toward the tree.

examples.ko: 오래 앉아 있었더니 다리가 아파서 어기적거려요.
examples.en: I sat for a long time and my legs hurt, so I'm walking stiffly.
The way the duck waddles is cute.
The child waddled around in big shoes.
Why are you walking so stiffly? Are you hurt?

explain: 몸이 무겁거나 다리가 불편해서 팔다리를 크게 움직이며 느리게 걷는 모습에 써요. 목적 없이 돌아다니는 '어슬렁거리다'와는 달리 걸음걸이가 둔하고 불편해 보일 때 말해요.

phrases.en: My knee hurts, so I walk with a stiff waddle.
phrases.nuance_ko: '어기적거리다'와 같은 뜻으로 바꿔 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Interchangeable with 어기적거리다.

phrases.en: I went up the stairs with a clumsy, waddling gait.
phrases.nuance_ko: 걸음걸이를 꾸미는 말로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to describe a way of walking.

phrases.en: I'm so full that I'm waddling.
phrases.nuance_ko: 몸이 무겁고 불편할 때 쓰는 해요체 활용이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The polite form for when your body feels heavy or uncomfortable.

explain_en: It describes walking slowly with big, heavy movements because the body is heavy or the legs are uncomfortable. Unlike '어슬렁거리다' (to wander about aimlessly), it focuses on a clumsy, awkward gait.

examples.ko: 아이가 빵을 입에 가득 넣고 우물우물 씹어요.
examples.en: The child chews bread slowly with a full mouth.

examples.ko: 그는 말해 놓고 우물우물 김치를 씹었어요.
examples.en: After saying it, he slowly chewed his kimchi.
Don't mumble your answer; say it clearly.

examples.ko: 할아버지가 우물우물 무슨 말씀을 하셨는데 잘 안 들렸어요.
examples.en: Grandfather mumbled something, but I couldn't hear it well.

examples.ko: 학생이 우물우물 변명을 늘어놓자 선생님이 한숨을 쉬셨어요.
examples.en: When the student mumbled out excuses, the teacher sighed.

examples.ko: 강아지가 간식을 우물우물 먹다가 나를 쳐다봤어요.
examples.en: The puppy chewed its treat and then looked at me.

explain: 입 안에서 천천히 씹는 모양과 말을 흐리는 모양, 두 가지에 써요. 단단한 것을 거칠게 씹는 '우적우적'과는 느낌이 달라요.

phrases.en: Grandmother chews her rice slowly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 음식을 입 안에서 천천히 씹을 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing for slowly chewing food in the mouth.

phrases.example: 그 사람은 우물우물 말해서 잘 안 들려요.
phrases.en: He mumbles, so I can't hear him well.
phrases.nuance_ko: 말소리가 흐릿하고 분명하지 않을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it when speech is blurry and unclear.

phrases.en: The child rolls a candy around in their mouth.
phrases.nuance_ko: 입 안에서 무언가를 천천히 움직이는 모습을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: It describes something being slowly moved around inside the mouth.
phrases.en_equiv: working something around in the mouth

explain_en: It is used for both slow chewing in the mouth and unclear mumbling. It feels different from '우적우적', which is for crunching hard food roughly.

en: to say thus and thus; to comment

examples.ko: 그는 내 실수를 운운하며 계속 화를 냈어요.
examples.en: He kept getting angry, going on about my mistake.

examples.ko: 아직 확실하지 않은데 벌써 결과를 운운하지 마세요.
examples.en: It's not certain yet, so don't talk about the results already.
My friend looked down on me, bringing up my age.

examples.ko: 월급을 운운하기 전에 맡은 일부터 하세요.
examples.en: Before you bring up your pay, do the work you were given.

examples.ko: 사람들이 뒤에서 내 성적을 운운하는 게 싫어요.
examples.en: I don't like people talking about my grades behind my back.

examples.ko: 그는 모임에서 늘 자기 학벌을 운운해요.
examples.en: At gatherings he is always bringing up his educational background.

explain: 'A를 운운하다'는 어떤 일을 이러쿵저러쿵 말하는 것인데, 말하는 사람이 못마땅하다는 느낌이 들어가요. 그래서 칭찬이나 좋은 이야기에는 잘 쓰지 않고, 불만이나 비난을 할 때 자주 나와요. 중립적으로 말하려면 '언급하다'를 써요.

phrases.example: 어른이 나이를 운운하며 제 의견을 무시했어요.
phrases.en: The adult brought up my age and ignored my opinion.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 것을 핑계나 이유로 들먹일 때 쓰고, 못마땅한 느낌이 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone harps on something as an excuse, with a disapproving tone.

phrases.example: 친구가 자꾸 돈을 운운해서 기분이 나빴어요.
phrases.en: My friend kept bringing up money, and I felt bad.
phrases.nuance_ko: 그 이야기를 불쾌하게 계속 꺼낸다는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Gives the feeling of unpleasantly bringing up a topic again and again.

phrases.example: 남의 일을 운운하는 사람은 별로 좋아하지 않아요.
phrases.en: I don't really like people who comment on other people's business.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이러쿵저러쿵 말하는 사람을 비판적으로 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used critically for a person who talks this and that about others.
phrases.en_equiv: a person who goes on about things

explain_en: 'A를 운운하다' means to talk about something this way and that, with a tone that the speaker disapproves. It is rarely used for praise or good news and often appears in complaints or criticism. For a neutral version, use '언급하다'.

examples.en: I confessed everything in front of the teacher.
If you come clean about the truth, I'll forgive you.

examples.ko: 동생이 컵을 깼다고 이실직고해서 안 혼났어요.
examples.en: My younger sibling admitted to breaking the cup, so he didn't get scolded.
It's better to come clean even now.
As soon as Mom asks, the child confesses right away.

examples.ko: 이실직고하지 않으면 계속 마음이 불편할 거예요.
examples.en: If you don't come clean, you'll keep feeling uneasy.

explain: 그냥 '솔직하게 말하다'가 아니라 숨기던 잘못을 털어놓을 때 써요. 친구나 가족 사이에서 "이실직고해!"처럼 장난스럽게 다그치는 말투로도 들을 수 있어요. 법적인 느낌이 강한 '자백하다'보다 가볍게 쓸 수 있어요.

phrases.en: Come clean about why you came home late yesterday!
phrases.nuance_ko: 잘못을 털어놓으라고 장난스럽게 다그치는 명령형이에요. 친구끼리는 '이실직고해!'라고 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A playful imperative demanding a confession; between friends people say '이실직고해!'.

phrases.en: In the end, I told the truth and apologized.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뜻이 비슷하고 대화에서 더 부드럽게 들려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar meaning, sounding softer in conversation.

phrases.en: The criminal confessed everything to the police.
phrases.nuance_ko: 법적인 느낌이 강해서 범죄나 수사 이야기에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Has a strong legal tone, used for crime and investigations.

explain_en: It is not just 'to speak honestly'; it is used when you own up to a fault you were hiding. Among friends and family you may hear it in a playfully pushy tone, like "이실직고해!". It can be used more lightly than '자백하다', which feels more legal.

examples.en: The spy's infiltration was only discovered later.
The reporter did undercover reporting inside the factory.

examples.ko: 경찰이 범인의 잠입 경로를 조사하고 있어요.
examples.en: The police are investigating the culprit's route of entry.

examples.ko: 영화 속 잠입 장면이 정말 긴장돼요.
examples.en: The infiltration scene in the movie is really tense.

examples.ko: 건물 경비는 잠입을 막으려고 문을 늘 잠가요.
examples.en: The building's guards always lock the doors to prevent anyone sneaking in.
The infiltration operation was carried out very quietly.

explain: 몰래 들어가는 일을 말해요. 영화, 뉴스, 수사 이야기에서 자주 나오고 '잠입 취재', '잠입 수사'처럼 목적이 있는 경우가 많아요. 그냥 몰래 들어가는 것은 '몰래 들어가다'가 더 자연스러워요.

phrases.en: The police caught the criminal through an undercover investigation.
phrases.nuance_ko: 신분을 숨기고 들어가 조사하는 일이에요. 영화와 뉴스에 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: An investigation done by entering with a hidden identity, common in films and news.

phrases.en: They succeeded in sneaking into the building.
phrases.nuance_ko: 들키지 않고 들어갔다는 뜻이에요. 이야기나 사건 설명에서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means getting in without being noticed, used in stories and incident reports.

phrases.en: The police are investigating the thief's route of entry.
phrases.nuance_ko: 몰래 들어온 길을 말해요. 사건 수사에서 자주 나오는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The path someone used to sneak in, common in crime investigations.

explain_en: It refers to entering somewhere secretly, and appears in films, news, and investigations, often in set phrases like 잠입 취재 (undercover reporting) and 잠입 수사 (undercover investigation). For plainly sneaking in, 몰래 들어가다 sounds more natural.

examples.en: People resisted the unfair order.
The child resists because they don't want to go to the hospital.
If you resist change, things get harder.
He didn't resist to the end.
I walked, pushing against the strong wind.
Germs that resist medicine are increasing.

explain: '버티다'는 참고 견디는 느낌이고, 저항하다는 상대의 힘이나 명령에 맞선다는 느낌이에요. 조사는 '~에 저항하다'를 써요. 명사 '저항'은 '저항이 크다', '저항을 받다'처럼 말해요.

phrases.en: They resisted to the end.
phrases.nuance_ko: 포기하지 않고 계속 맞선다는 느낌을 더하는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A pairing that adds the sense of never giving up.

phrases.example: 너무 갑자기 일어난 일이라서 저항하지 못했어요.
phrases.en: It happened so suddenly that I couldn't resist.
phrases.nuance_ko: 맞서고 싶어도 못 했다는 뜻의 부정 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A negative expression meaning you wanted to resist but couldn't.

phrases.en: There is strong resistance to the new rule.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 '저항'을 써서 반대하는 힘의 크기를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Uses the noun 저항 to describe how strong the opposition is.

explain_en: '버티다' is about enduring, while 저항하다 is about standing against someone's force or order. The particle is '에', as in '~에 저항하다'. The noun '저항' appears in '저항이 크다' and '저항을 받다'.

t90.ax: He didn't resist to the end.

examples.ko: 어제 회식에서 추태를 부린 게 너무 부끄러워요.
examples.en: I'm so embarrassed about making a scene at the company dinner yesterday.

examples.ko: 길에서 추태를 부리는 사람을 보면 눈살이 찌푸려져요.
examples.en: I frown when I see someone behaving shamefully on the street.

examples.ko: 팬들의 추태가 뉴스에 나와서 모두가 놀랐어요.
examples.en: Everyone was shocked when the fans' ugly behavior was on the news.

examples.ko: 그 선수는 경기 중에 보인 추태 때문에 사과했어요.
examples.en: The player apologized for his unseemly behavior during the game.

examples.ko: 더 이상 추태는 못 보겠으니 이제 그만하세요.
examples.en: I can't stand any more of this disgraceful behavior, so please stop now.

examples.ko: 친구가 한 추태를 누가 사진으로 찍어 놓았대요.
examples.en: Apparently someone took a photo of my friend's embarrassing behavior.

explain: '실수'와 달리 체면을 잃을 만큼 보기 흉하고 창피한 행동을 비난하는 느낌이 강해요. '추태를 부리다', '추태를 보이다'처럼 말하고, 남의 행동에 쓰는 경우가 많아서 자기 행동에 쓰면 많이 부끄러워하는 말투가 돼요.

phrases.example: 술에 취해 추태를 부리면 안 돼요.
phrases.en: You shouldn't make a scene when you're drunk.
phrases.nuance_ko: 보기 흉한 행동을 했다고 비난할 때 가장 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing for criticizing disgraceful behavior.

phrases.en: I'm sorry for behaving badly in front of the guests.
phrases.nuance_ko: 남에게 창피한 모습을 보였다는 뜻으로, 사과할 때도 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means showing an embarrassing side to others; can be used when apologizing.

phrases.example: 술자리 추태는 다음 날 후회가 돼요.
phrases.en: Bad behavior at a drinking party leads to regret the next day.
phrases.nuance_ko: 술에 취해서 하는 흉한 행동을 말할 때 자주 붙는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common phrase for disgraceful behavior while drunk.

explain_en: Unlike '실수' (a mistake), it carries a strong tone of criticism for behavior so unseemly that someone loses face. It is used as '추태를 부리다' or '추태를 보이다', and mostly about other people's behavior. Using it about yourself sounds deeply ashamed.

examples.ko: 뜨거운 국물을 후후 불어 가며 먹었어요.
examples.en: I ate the hot soup, blowing on it as I went.

examples.ko: 아이가 생일 케이크의 촛불을 후후 불었어요.
examples.en: The child blew out the candles on the birthday cake with a puff puff.

examples.ko: 추운 날 손을 후후 불면 조금 따뜻해져요.
examples.en: On a cold day, if you blow on your hands, they get a little warmer.

examples.ko: 엄마가 아픈 곳에 후후 해 주셨어요.
examples.en: Mom blew gently on the sore spot for me.
The ramyeon is hot, so I eat it while cooling it with my breath.

examples.ko: 그는 하얀 입김을 후후 내뱉으며 걸었어요.
examples.en: He walked, puffing out white breath.

explain: 입으로 바람을 짧게 여러 번 부는 소리나 모습이에요. 뜨거운 음식을 식히거나 손을 녹일 때 '후후 불다'로 자주 써요. 한 번 세게 부는 느낌이면 '후' 하고 불다라고 해요.

phrases.example: 엄마가 아픈 곳을 후후 불어 줘요.
phrases.en: Mom blows on the sore spot for me.
phrases.nuance_ko: 다친 곳이나 뜨거운 음식을 남을 위해 불어 줄 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when blowing on a sore spot or hot food for someone else.

phrases.en: I blow on the hot porridge to cool it down.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뜨거운 음식을 식히는 목적을 함께 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it to say you blow on food in order to cool it.

phrases.en: It was cold, so I blew on my hands.
phrases.nuance_ko: 추울 때 손을 녹이는 모습에 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing for warming cold hands with your breath.

explain_en: It imitates short, repeated puffs of breath from the mouth. It is often used as '후후 불다' when cooling hot food or warming hands. For a single stronger blow, people say '후' instead.

t90.ax: He walked, puffing out white breath.

en: to be swung; to be wielded; to be brandished

examples.ko: 저는 남의 말에 쉽게 휘둘리는 편이에요.
examples.en: I tend to be easily swayed by what other people say.
Don't be ruled by your emotions; think calmly.

examples.ko: 친구에게 휘둘리다 보니 제 시간이 없어요.
examples.en: Since I get pushed around by my friend, I have no time of my own.

examples.ko: 유행에 휘둘리고 싶지 않아서 천천히 샀어요.
examples.en: I didn't want to be swept up by trends, so I bought slowly.

examples.ko: 주식 가격에 휘둘릴 때마다 마음이 불안했어요.
examples.en: Every time I was thrown around by stock prices, I felt anxious.

examples.ko: 소문에 휘둘리면 진짜 중요한 걸 놓쳐요.
examples.en: If you get carried away by rumors, you miss what really matters.

explain: '휘두르다'(막 흔들다)의 피동형이지만 실제로는 '남이나 감정에 끌려다니다'라는 뜻으로 더 많이 써요. 보통 '○○에 휘둘리다'로 쓰고, 좋은 뜻은 아니에요. 반대로 줏대가 있는 사람은 '중심을 잡다'라고 해요.

phrases.en: When you are angry, it's easy to be swayed by your emotions.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기분에 끌려서 차분하게 행동하지 못할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you can't act calmly because your feelings pull you around.

phrases.en: I'm having a hard time being pushed around by my friends.
phrases.nuance_ko: 남의 뜻대로 계속 끌려다닐 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you keep being dragged along by others' wishes.

phrases.en: To avoid being shaken, you need to keep your balance.
phrases.nuance_ko: '휘둘리다'의 반대로, 줏대 있게 흔들리지 않는다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The opposite of 휘둘리다: staying steady and not being swayed.

explain_en: It comes from 휘두르다 (to wave around), but in practice it mostly means being dragged along by other people or emotions. The usual form is ○○에 휘둘리다, and it has a negative tone. Someone with a firm mind is described with 중심을 잡다.

en: to fizzle out; to peter out

examples.en: If you leave work half-done and vague, you lose trust.
He always leaves his assigned tasks vaguely unfinished.
He did his homework sloppily and went out to play.
The problem was brushed aside, so it eventually got bigger.

examples.ko: 약속을 흐지부지하지 말고 분명히 말해 주세요.
examples.en: Please don't be vague about the promise; tell me clearly.
I have many plans that I started and left hanging.

explain: 일을 분명히 마무리하지 않고 얼버무리거나 대충 끝내는 것을 말해요. 저절로 슬그머니 사라지는 건 '흐지부지되다'라고 하고, 일상에서는 '흐지부지 넘어가다'처럼 부사로 더 자주 써요.

phrases.en: When a question comes up, he glosses over it.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상에서 '흐지부지하다'보다 더 자주 쓰는 부사 형태예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The adverb form, more common in daily speech than the verb.

phrases.en: You shouldn't finish your homework half-heartedly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일을 대충 마무리할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when wrapping up a task sloppily.

phrases.en: When I ask him why, he mumbles and dodges.
phrases.nuance_ko: 말을 분명하게 하지 않고 얼버무리는 모습을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes mumbling and being unclear when speaking.

explain_en: It describes leaving something vague or half-done instead of finishing it properly. When something fades away by itself, use '흐지부지되다', and in daily talk the adverb is more common, as in '흐지부지 넘어가다'.

t90.ax: He did his homework sloppily and went out to play.

examples.en: My father wears long sideburns.
My sideburns are long, so I need to go to the barber.
That actor's sideburns look cool.
The sideburns run from in front of the ear down to the chin.
Now that you've grown sideburns too, you look different.

examples.ko: 구레나룻에 흰 털이 조금 섞여 있어요.
examples.en: There are a few white hairs mixed into the sideburns.

explain: 귀 밑에서 턱까지 이어서 난 수염을 말해요. 입 위의 '콧수염', 턱에 난 '턱수염'과 구별해서 써요. 발음은 [구레나룯]이에요.

phrases.en: He is growing sideburns.
phrases.nuance_ko: 수염을 일부러 길게 놔둘 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you leave facial hair to grow long on purpose.

phrases.en: I got my sideburns cut short at the barbershop.
phrases.nuance_ko: 면도하거나 짧게 정리할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for shaving or trimming them short.

phrases.example: 동생은 고등학생 때 벌써 구레나룻이 났어요.
phrases.en: My younger brother already had sideburns coming in when he was in high school.
phrases.nuance_ko: 수염이 자라서 생겼다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means the facial hair has grown in.

explain_en: This is the beard growing from below the ears down to the chin. Keep it separate from '콧수염' (mustache) and '턱수염' (chin beard). It is pronounced [구레나룯].

en: to be bent; to be curved

examples.en: Grandpa's back is bent, so he uses a cane.

examples.ko: 꾸부정한 자세로 오래 앉아 있으면 허리가 아파요.
examples.en: If you sit for long in a hunched posture, your back hurts.
He walks stooped over, so I worry about his health.
Your shoulders are hunched, so try straightening them.

examples.ko: 키 큰 학생이 꾸부정하게 서 있었어요.
examples.en: The tall student was standing with a stoop.
His back has become hunched as he got older.

explain: 허리, 어깨, 등처럼 몸이 앞으로 약간 굽은 모양을 말해요. 자세가 좋지 않다는 느낌이 있어서 '쭉 펴세요'와 자주 같이 나와요. '구부정하다'와 같은 말인데 더 센 느낌이에요.

phrases.example: 꾸부정한 자세로 앉아 있으면 목도 아파요.
phrases.en: Sitting in a hunched posture hurts your neck too.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-ㄴ'을 붙여 자세를 꾸밀 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: With -ㄴ it describes a posture.

phrases.en: I use the computer a lot, so my shoulders are hunched.
phrases.nuance_ko: 허리뿐 아니라 어깨와 등이 굽은 모양에도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for shoulders and back as well as the waist.

phrases.en: My father's back is a bit stooped these days.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뜻은 같고 '꾸부정하다'보다 느낌이 약해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning, but weaker than 꾸부정하다.

explain_en: It describes the body, such as the back or shoulders, bending slightly forward. It carries a feeling of poor posture, so it often appears with phrases like '쭉 펴세요' (straighten up). It is the same word as '구부정하다' but sounds stronger.

t90.ax: Grandpa's back is bent, so he uses a cane.

examples.ko: 매일 신은 운동화 뒤축이 한쪽만 닳았어요.
examples.en: The heel of the sneakers I wear every day is worn down on one side only.
The heels of my shoes were worn down, so I went to get them repaired.
There's a hole in the heel of my sock.

examples.ko: 신발 뒤축을 구겨 신으면 발이 아파요.
examples.en: If you wear shoes with the heel folded down, your feet hurt.

examples.ko: 새 신발이라 뒤축이 발에 쓸려서 아파요.
examples.en: They're new shoes, so the back rubs against my foot and hurts.

examples.ko: 뒤축이 단단한 신발은 발을 잘 잡아 줘요.
examples.en: Shoes with a firm heel counter hold your foot well.

explain: 신발이나 양말의 뒤쪽 부분을 말해요. 땅에 닿는 높은 부분은 '굽'이나 '뒷굽'이라고 하고, 발 자체의 뒤쪽은 보통 '뒤꿈치'라고 해요.

phrases.en: I've worn these shoes for so long that the heels are worn down.
phrases.nuance_ko: 신발을 오래 신으면 뒤쪽이 먼저 닳아서 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pair, since the back of a shoe often wears out first.

phrases.en: There is a hole in the heel of my sock.
phrases.nuance_ko: 신발뿐 아니라 양말의 뒤쪽 부분에도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the back part of socks as well as shoes.

phrases.example: 신발 뒤축을 꺾어 신으면 발에 안 좋아요.
phrases.en: Wearing shoes with the heel folded down is bad for your feet.
phrases.nuance_ko: 신발 뒤쪽을 접어서 슬리퍼처럼 신는 것을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means folding down the back of a shoe to wear it like a slipper.
phrases.en_equiv: to wear shoes with the heel folded down

explain_en: It refers to the back part of a shoe or sock. The raised part that touches the ground is called 굽 or 뒷굽, and the back of the foot itself is usually called 뒤꿈치.

t90.ax: There's a hole in the heel of my sock.

examples.en: My younger sibling has buck teeth and is getting braces.
Her buck teeth show a little when she smiles.
I worried about my buck teeth when I was little.
I had my buck teeth fixed at a dentist's office in a big hospital.
They say that actor's buck teeth are his charm.
The child with buck teeth smiled broadly.

explain: 앞니가 바깥쪽으로 튀어나온 이를 말해요. 놀리는 말처럼 들릴 수 있어서 상대방 앞에서는 조심해서 써야 해요. '덧니'는 이가 겹쳐서 하나 더 난 것이라서 서로 다른 말이에요.

phrases.en: My younger sibling has buck teeth and wears braces.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이가 튀어나온 상태를 말할 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common collocation for having protruding teeth.

phrases.en: I had my buck teeth corrected when I was young.
phrases.nuance_ko: 치과에서 이를 바로잡는 일을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for dental treatment that straightens the teeth.

phrases.en: My front teeth stick out a little.
phrases.nuance_ko: '뻐드렁니'보다 부드럽고 덜 놀리는 느낌으로 말할 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: A gentler way to say it that sounds less teasing than 'ppeodeureongni'.

explain_en: It refers to front teeth that stick out. It can sound like teasing, so be careful using it in front of someone. '덧니' is different: it means an extra tooth growing out of line.

examples.ko: 저는 어릴 때부터 약골이라서 감기를 자주 앓았어요.
examples.en: I've been frail since I was little, so I often caught colds.

examples.ko: 그렇게 약골처럼 굴지 말고 운동 좀 해요.
examples.en: Stop acting like such a weakling and get some exercise.
My older brother was frail, but he built up his body through exercise.
I thought he was a weakling, but he finished the marathon.

examples.ko: 우리 팀에서 약골 소리를 듣던 막내가 오늘 이겼어요.
examples.en: The youngest, who was called a weakling on our team, won today.
He may look frail, but he's surprisingly strong.

explain: 몸이 약한 사람을 가리키는 말인데, 놀리는 말투나 친한 사이의 농담으로 자주 써요. 면전에서 남에게 말하면 기분 나빠할 수 있어서 조심해야 해요. 중립적으로 말할 때는 '몸이 약한 편이다', '허약 체질이다'를 써요.

phrases.en: I'm a weakling, so even a short walk tires me out.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자기 자신을 농담처럼 말할 때 쓰기 좋아요.
phrases.nuance_en: Good for joking about yourself.

phrases.example: 어릴 때 약골 소리를 자주 들었어요.
phrases.en: I often got called a weakling when I was young.
phrases.nuance_ko: 남들에게서 몸이 약하다는 말을 들었다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means others often said you were physically weak.

phrases.example: 저는 허약 체질이라 겨울마다 감기에 걸려요.
phrases.en: I have a weak constitution, so I catch a cold every winter.
phrases.nuance_ko: '약골'보다 부드럽고 중립적으로 몸이 약하다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A softer, neutral way to say someone is physically weak.

explain_en: It refers to a physically weak person and is often used as teasing or a joke between close friends. Saying it to someone's face can upset them, so be careful. For a neutral way to say it, use '몸이 약한 편이다' or '허약 체질이다'.
